feature_request: Improve the Release Manager review console's visual design and usability without changing any behavior, routes, or the CLI-invocation logic. Specifically: replace the current plain HTML with a proper light/dark-aware visual design (color palette, spacing, typography) using only inline CSS in server.js's existing layout() function; give each of the seven actions (Configure, Scan, Prepare, Recover, Approve, Reject, Publish) a distinct visual affordance (icon or color) reflecting whether it's safe, cautionary, or destructive; show a persistent status indicator (last exit code, last action, timestamp) in the page header/nav so the operator doesn't have to scroll to /audit to see recent activity; and improve the process-result page so stdout/stderr are visually distinguished from each other and collapsible when long, instead of two flat <pre> blocks. Do not add any client-side JavaScript, external stylesheets, or frameworks — all styling must remain inline CSS shipped with the existing server-rendered HTML, consistent with the current zero-dependency, no-build-step design.

output.title: Refresh the Release Manager review console presentation and activity visibility
output.description: Update the existing server-rendered review console with an embedded light/dark-aware design, distinct action affordances, a layout-wide recent-activity indicator, and clearer collapsible process output while preserving all existing behavior, routes, and CLI invocation logic.
requirements: R1: Replace the console's plain presentation with a coherent visual design covering color palette, spacing, and typography.
R2: Implement all visual styling as CSS embedded by server.js's existing layout() function so every page using that layout receives the design.
R3: Make the embedded design light/dark-aware, including an appropriate dark palette selected through CSS such as the prefers-color-scheme media query.
R4: Give each of Configure, Scan, Prepare, Recover, Approve, Reject, and Publish its own visually distinguishable affordance using an icon, color, or both.

R5: The action affordances must communicate safe, cautionary, or destructive intent. The feature request does not prescribe the exact risk-category assignment, icon, or color for every action; those choices must remain consistent with each action's existing meaning, and actions in the same risk category must still be individually distinguishable.
R6: Render a persistent recent-activity indicator in the shared page header or navigation area showing the last action, its exit code, and its timestamp.
R7: When recorded activity exists, the indicator must display the values from the most recent established activity result rather than requiring the operator to visit or scroll through /audit.
R8: When no recorded activity exists, the header or navigation must still contain a non-misleading empty-state status indicator rather than presenting invented action, exit-code, or timestamp values.
R9: On process-result pages, present stdout and stderr as separately labeled and visually distinct streams rather than as two undifferentiated flat preformatted blocks.

R10: Long stdout and stderr content must be independently collapsible using server-rendered native HTML controls, such as separate details/summary elements, so no client-side JavaScript is required. The request does not specify the exact length threshold; it must be deterministic, and clearly large content must receive the collapsible treatment.
R11: Preserve the actual stdout and stderr text shown to the operator, including the existing escaping and output semantics; the change is to presentation and collapsibility only.

R12: Preserve all existing application behavior, route paths, accepted request shapes, action semantics, CLI arguments, CLI argument ordering, subprocess invocation logic, result handling, and audit behavior.
constraints: C1: Changes are limited to server.js.
C2: CSS must be shipped inside the existing server-rendered HTML through layout(); no external stylesheet may be introduced.
C3: Do not add client-side JavaScript.
C4: Do not add frameworks, packages, build tools, or runtime dependencies; retain the current zero-dependency, no-build-step design.
C5: Do not add, remove, rename, or redirect routes.
C6: Do not alter the logic that maps the seven actions to CLI invocations, including executable selection, argument-array contents or ordering, working-directory behavior, or environment handling.
C7: Do not alter action execution, process-result, error, or audit semantics while changing the generated HTML presentation.

C8: The exact colors, icons, typography values, spacing values, timestamp format, no-activity wording, and long-output threshold are not specified by the request and must not be treated as fixed interfaces beyond satisfying the stated visual and informational requirements.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 [R1, R2, R3, C2]: HTML produced through layout() contains an embedded style element defining the console's palette, spacing, and typography, plus a light/dark-aware CSS rule; rendered pages do not reference an external stylesheet.

AC2 [R4, R5]: The rendered controls for Configure, Scan, Prepare, Recover, Approve, Reject, and Publish each have an observable, individually distinguishable icon and/or color treatment, and their styling visibly differentiates safe, cautionary, and destructive intent.

AC3 [R6, R7]: After an action has a recorded result, every relevant page rendered through the shared layout—including the resulting process page and /audit—shows a header or navigation status area containing that most recent action's action name, exit code, and timestamp.

AC4 [R8]: With no recorded activity available, pages rendered through the shared layout still show a status area that clearly indicates the absence of recent activity and does not fabricate an exit code or timestamp.

AC5 [R9, R11]: A process result containing both stdout and stderr renders two clearly labeled regions with visibly different presentation, and each region contains the corresponding original escaped stream text without swapping or merging the streams.

AC6 [R10, C3]: For a process result whose stdout and stderr are each clearly large, each stream is independently contained in a native server-rendered collapsible control with a visible summary or label; expanding or collapsing one stream does not require JavaScript or control the other stream.

AC7 [R12, C5, C6, C7]: All pre-existing route and action tests continue to pass, and the seven actions retain their existing request handling, CLI argument arrays and ordering, result outcomes, and audit effects.
AC8 [C2, C3, C4]: server.js introduces no external CSS or script references, client-side script, framework import, package dependency, or build-step requirement.
AC9 [C1]: The implementation changes no project file other than server.js.
out_of_scope: Changing CLI workflow or invocation logic.
Adding, removing, renaming, or otherwise changing routes.
Changing action behavior, process execution semantics, or audit semantics.
Adding client-side interactivity implemented with JavaScript.
Adding external stylesheets, UI frameworks, packages, dependencies, or a build step.
Defining a new exact public programmatic interface; this feature changes only the existing server-rendered presentation.

output.explanation: The failing assertions incorrectly require HTTP 200 for deliberately configured nonzero subprocess exit codes (Reject exit 27 and Scan exit 23). The implementation correctly preserves established result handling by treating nonzero CLI exits as failed process results and returning HTTP 500 while still rendering/auditing the result. This is consistent with C7/R12, which require preserving result handling. The test therefore rejects the intended scenario before checking the presentation behavior it claims to cover. Its Reject expectation of a --reason CLI argument also conflicts with the rendered Reject form and is not established by this presentation-only contract.
output.feedback_for_verifier: Update the action and large-stream tests to expect HTTP 500 when their fixture configures a nonzero exitCode, then continue asserting rendered stdout/stderr, audit persistence, activity status, and CLI invocation. Do not require Reject to accept/forward a reason or invoke ['reject','--reason',... ] unless that behavior is established by the pre-existing implementation contract; this UI-change contract explicitly requires preserving existing request shapes and invocation mappings.

output.explanation: The status indicator falsely reports an empty audit history when activity data cannot be read due to permission or other I/O failures. That is misleading recent-activity visibility and violates the request's usability goal as well as the contract's non-misleading empty-state requirement. A genuine absence of an audit file may be shown as no activity, but operational read failures require a distinct unavailable/error state.

patterns: When tests exercise deliberately failed subprocess outcomes, assert the established failure semantics (such as HTTP 500) while still checking rendered output and auditing; do not infer new request fields or CLI arguments that the existing contract never defined.

Distinguish a genuinely absent persistence file from an operational read failure: absence can produce an honest empty state, but permission, parsing, or other I/O failures require a separate unavailable/error state rather than silently reporting no data.

For shared activity indicators backed by append-only logs, read from the newest entries backward, skip malformed records, and display the most recent valid established result without fabricating values when none exists.

For server-rendered process output, keep stdout and stderr independently labeled, escaped, visually distinct, and independently collapsible with native HTML controls so presentation changes do not alter output semantics or require client-side JavaScript.
